from_notes: Anions: They are negatively charged ions formed when an atom gains electrons
x: A body becomes negatively charged by gaining electrons; protons are not transferred in charging.

from_notes: Prokaryotic cell: No membrane-bound organelles
x: Prokaryotes lack membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria, but have a cell wall, plasma membrane and ribosomes.

from_notes: plant cells have a unique cell wall
x: Every plant cell has a cellulose cell wall, which animal cells lack, so the cell wall is the safest answer. Chloroplasts are also plant-only but are absent from roots and other non-green cells, and cell membrane and nucleus occur in both.

from_notes: The plasma membrane is flexible and is made up of organic molecules called lipids and proteins
x: The plasma membrane is made of lipids and proteins and has no nucleic acid; the nucleolus, chloroplast and ribosome contain RNA or DNA.

Chloroplasts have their own DNA and ribosomes and divide independently, so they are called a cell within a cell (the same is said of mitochondria, which are not offered). Ribosomes, lysosomes and Golgi bodies have no DNA of their own.
source: NCERT Biology Class 11 ch.8 (Cell: semi-autonomous chloroplast/mitochondria); printed key NDA 2007, not verified against another key

from_notes: Active Transport: It uses energy to move substances against their concentration gradient
x: Active transport moves ions against the concentration gradient and requires energy (ATP); diffusion is passive.

from_notes: The nucleolus is a dense, spherical structure. It is a site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis.
x: The nucleolus is the site where ribosomal RNA is made and ribosomes are assembled; the Golgi bodies, ER and plasma membrane do not form ribosomes.

from_notes: Oxidation is the gain of oxygen or loss of hydrogen. Reduction is the loss of oxygen or gain of hydrogen.
x: By the OIL RIG rule oxidation is loss (of electrons, and of hydrogen), so loss of hydrogen is oxidation, not reduction.

from_notes: Reduction: Gain of electrons
x: By OIL RIG, oxidation is electron loss, so gain of electrons is reduction.

from_notes: Oxidation is the gain of oxygen or loss of hydrogen. Reduction is the loss of oxygen or gain of hydrogen.
x: Loss of oxygen from a substance is reduction, the opposite of oxidation (gain of oxygen); corrosion is a different process.
In electroplating the object to be plated (the spoon) is made the cathode and the plating metal (pure nickel) is the anode, so nickel dissolves from the anode and deposits on the spoon.
source: NCERT Science Class 8 ch.14 Chemical Effects of Electric Current (electroplating)

x: The energy needed to remove the electron from hydrogen's ground state is 13.6 eV (electron-volts), not MeV or J.
source: NCERT Physics Class 12 ch.12 Atoms (E1 = -13.6 eV)

from_notes: Energy can neither be created nor destroyed; only transformed
x: Creating something from nothing would violate the law of conservation of mass-energy, which says mass-energy can be neither created nor destroyed.
Kirchhoff's loop rule says the net energy gained and lost by a charge around a closed loop is zero, which is conservation of energy.
source: NCERT Physics Class 12 ch.3 Current Electricity (Kirchhoff's rules)

from_notes: Violet Maximum deviation (highest n)
x: Violet light has the shortest wavelength and highest refractive index in glass, so it bends (deviates) the most in a prism; red deviates the least.

from_notes: Fertilisation or syngamy involves the fusion of male and female gametes to form a diploid zygote.
x: Syngamy is the fusion of gametes, a feature of sexual reproduction; budding, gemmulation and fragmentation are asexual methods.

from_notes: Paramecium Protista
x: Paramecium is a unicellular protozoan; fungi (mostly), Spirogyra and Hydra are multicellular.

from_notes: Collenchyma cells ... have thickened corners due to extra cellulose, hemicellulose, and pectin
x: Collenchyma has cell corners thickened with cellulose and pectin, giving flexible support; lignin is characteristic of sclerenchyma.
n-Butane and isobutane share the formula C4H10 but differ in carbon chain (straight vs branched), so they are chain isomers.
source: NCERT Chemistry Class 11 ch.12 Organic Chemistry (structural isomerism)

from_notes: Active Transport: It uses energy to move substances against their concentration gradient
x: Active transport moves a substance against its concentration gradient using energy (ATP) from respiration; movement along the gradient or without energy is diffusion or passive transport.

from_notes: Photosynthesis is a process where green plants transform sunlight (light energy) into chemical energy
x: Plants prepare their food by photosynthesis, using light, CO2 and water in chlorophyll-containing cells.

from_notes: Photosynthesis occurs in the chloroplasts, primarily in plant leaves.
x: Photosynthesis occurs in chloroplasts, which contain chlorophyll; mitochondria are for respiration.

A grasshopper's hearing organs (tympana) are on the sides of the first abdominal segment, i.e. the abdomen, which the options call 'stomach'. Crickets and katydids have them on the front legs, not grasshoppers.
source: Britannica 'Orthopteran: tympanal organs' (grasshoppers: on the first abdominal segment); printed key SSC CGL 2019

from_notes: Apical meristems are found at the tips of roots and stems. They are responsible for primary growth
x: Apical meristems at the tips of stems and roots cause increase in length (primary growth); lateral meristem increases girth.
The first law of thermodynamics states that energy cannot be created or destroyed, which is the law of conservation of energy applied to heat and work.

from_notes: Refrigerator: Heat is extracted from cold body (inside) and rejected to hot body; Based on Second Law of Thermodynamics (external work required)
x: The Kelvin-Clausius statement that heat cannot flow spontaneously from cold to hot body is the Second Law of Thermodynamics.

from_notes: Energy Transport Waves transfer energy without transferring matter
x: Sound waves transmit only energy through a medium; the particles just oscillate about their mean positions and no matter is carried along.
Burning of natural gas, respiration and composting all release heat, so all are exothermic reactions.
source: NCERT Science Class 10 ch.1 Chemical Reactions and Equations (respiration and composting are exothermic)

x: Marsilea is a pteridophyte and has xylem and phloem. Cladophora and Anabaena are algae and Penicillium is a fungus, so none of them has vascular tissue.
source: NCERT Science Class 9 ch.7 Diversity / NCERT Biology Class 11 ch.3 Plant Kingdom (Marsilea a pteridophyte)

x: Transferring charge from a charged body to the Earth is called earthing (grounding).
source: NCERT Science Class 8 ch.15 Some Natural Phenomena (earthing)

from_notes: Pteridophytes possess vascular tissues (xylem and phloem). E.g., horsetails and ferns.
x: Marsilea, ferns and horsetails (Equisetum) are all seedless vascular plants, so they belong to Pteridophyta.

from_notes: Pteridophytes possess vascular tissues (xylem and phloem). E.g., horsetails and ferns.
x: Ferns and fern allies (horsetails, club mosses) make up the Pteridophyta.

from_notes: Maximum water absorbed by plants Root hairs
x: Roots are the main absorbing organs of plants, taking up water and minerals from the soil through root hairs.

from_notes: pigments like anthocyanins
x: Anthocyanins are water-soluble pigments that give red, pink, blue and purple colours to flowers. Carotenoids give yellow and orange.

from_notes: Earliest/oldest organism on Earth Blue-green algae (Cyanobacteria)
x: Blue-green algae (cyanobacteria) are among the earliest life forms, appearing about 3.5 billion years ago.

from_notes: Burning of paper / wood / candle Ash, CO2, H2O formed (chemical change)
x: Burning a candle is combustion, which releases heat and light, so it is exothermic. It is also a chemical change, not a physical one.
Transistors are used in amplifier circuits such as hearing aids. A fuse is a simple heating-effect wire and a fluorescent lamp is a gas discharge tube.
source: NCERT Physics Class 12 ch.14 Semiconductor Electronics (transistor as amplifier)

x: Fasciola is at organ level, Spongilla at cellular level, Obelia at tissue level and Pheretima at organ-system level, giving the code 2 3 4 1.
source: NCERT Biology Class 11 ch.4 Animal Kingdom (levels of organisation)

x: Cytology is the scientific study of cells. Histology studies tissues and taxonomy deals with classification.
source: NCERT Biology Class 11 ch.1 / standard definitions

from_notes: are generally oviparous (animals that lay eggs)
x: A frog lays eggs, so it is oviparous. Rabbit, mouse and squirrel are mammals that give birth to young.

from_notes: Bryophytes: E.g., Funaria, Polytrichum and Sphagnum (no vascular tissue)
x: Bryophytes lack a vascular system (xylem and phloem). Thallophytes lack a differentiated body, Funaria is a moss, and pteridophytes are cryptogams, not phanerogams.
Pteridophytes have vascular tissue but no seeds or flowers, so they are called vascular cryptogams.
source: NCERT Biology Class 11 ch.3 Plant Kingdom (pteridophytes = vascular cryptogams)

x: Primitive vascular plants had a protostele, in which the xylem forms a solid core surrounded by phloem.
source: Standard botany (Vashishta/Pandey Pteridophyta: protostele most primitive); printed key IAS 2017, not verified

x: A snail is a mollusc, an invertebrate with no backbone. Mammals, fish and birds are vertebrates.
source: NCERT Biology Class 11 ch.4 Animal Kingdom

from_notes: They have a three-chambered heart (two auricles and one ventricle)
x: Amphibians such as salamanders have a three-chambered heart. Scoliodon (fish) has two chambers, while pigeon and human have four.

from_notes: A flower is a modified shoot where the growing tip (shoot apical meristem) turns into a floral meristem
x: A flower is a modified shoot, formed from the shoot apical meristem, with its parts as modified leaves.

from_notes: Gymnosperms have exposed ovules and naked seeds.
x: Gymnosperms (e.g., pines, cycads) bear naked seeds not enclosed in an ovary or fruit; angiosperms have seeds inside fruits.

from_notes: Leopard Panthera pardus
x: Panthera pardus is the leopard; the tiger is Panthera tigris and the lion is Panthera leo. Panther is a general term for leopards/black panthers.

from_notes: They have a two-chambered heart and are cold-blooded (poikilothermic)
x: Shark is a fish and therefore cold-blooded (poikilothermic), whereas dolphins, whales and porpoises are mammals and warm-blooded.
An endothermic reaction absorbs heat from its surroundings, such as the decomposition of calcium carbonate on heating. A reaction that releases heat is exothermic.
source: NCERT Science Class 10 ch.1 Chemical Reactions and Equations (endothermic reaction absorbs heat)

from_notes: CO2 Heavier than air, acidic oxide Non-toxic in low conc.; asphyxiant in high
x: CO2 is an acidic oxide (forms carbonic acid with water) and turns lime water milky due to calcium carbonate formation. It is not poisonous, only an asphyxiant at high concentration, so statement I is wrong.
In an X-ray tube only about 1% of the electron energy becomes X-rays, and the rest is converted to heat at the target, so heat is generated there.
source: NCERT Physics Class 12 ch.11 Dual Nature / standard X-ray tube physics

x: Methane (firedamp) mixes with air in coal mines and forms an explosive mixture; CO2 and nitrogen are not flammable.
source: NCERT Science Class 8 ch.5 Coal and Petroleum / standard (firedamp)

x: Oxygen is directly used as the final electron acceptor in the electron transport chain; glycolysis and fermentation are anaerobic, and the citric acid cycle uses oxygen only indirectly.
source: NCERT Biology Class 11 ch.14 Respiration in Plants (oxygen as final electron acceptor)

x: Moving left to right across a period, electrons and protons increase by one per element, but the number of shells (the period number) stays the same.
source: NCERT Science Class 10 ch.5 Periodic Classification

x: The cut-off wavelength is λ = hc/eV, so it is inversely proportional to the applied potential; doubling V halves the cut-off wavelength.
source: NCERT Physics Class 12 ch.11 Dual Nature (λmin = hc/eV)

x: Ice is just solid water, a pure compound, so it is not a mixture; ice-cream, air and honey are mixtures of several components.
source: NCERT Science Class 9 ch.2 Is Matter Around Us Pure

from_notes: Anomalous Expansion Water contracts on heating from 0°C to 4°C
x: Water contracts, not expands, when heated from 0°C to 4°C (anomalous expansion of water), so the statement about ice expanding uniformly up to 4°C is incorrect.

from_notes: a hypertonic solution is more concentrated (plasmolysis)
x: Water moves by osmosis from low to high solute concentration through a semi-permeable membrane. A cell in a more concentrated medium therefore loses water and shrinks.

from_notes: State Solid (except mercury)
x: Mercury is the only metal liquid at room temperature; lead, sodium and calcium are solids.

from_notes: State Solid (except mercury)
x: Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature; cadmium, germanium and tin are solids.
Hexane is a saturated alkane with a low carbon percentage and burns with a clean flame. Benzene, naphthalene and anthracene are aromatic and carbon-rich, so they burn with a sooty flame.
source: NCERT Science Class 10 ch.4 Carbon and its Compounds (combustion)

from_notes: Malic acid C4H6O5 Apples
x: Apples contain malic acid; nitric and sulphuric acids are strong mineral acids not found in fruits, and formic acid is found in ant stings.
Ripe bananas contain malic acid as their main organic acid; formic acid occurs in ants and the others are mineral acids.
source: Food-chemistry references (USDA/food science: malic acid predominant in banana pulp); printed key SSC 2019, not verified against a library source

x: In the Calvin cycle CO2 combines with RuBP to give 3-phosphoglyceric acid (PGA), the first stable product of carbon fixation. Glucose and starch form later.
source: NCERT Biology Class 11 ch.13 Photosynthesis (Calvin cycle: 3-PGA first stable product)

x: Glycolysis breaks down glucose into two molecules of pyruvic acid (pyruvate). Ethanol and CO2 form only afterwards in fermentation.
source: NCERT Biology Class 11 ch.14 Respiration in Plants (glycolysis ends in pyruvic acid)

x: SO2 has sulphur in the +4 state, so it can be oxidised to +6 or reduced to lower states and acts as both. H2 and HI act mainly as reducing agents, and H2S too.
source: NCERT Chemistry Class 11 ch.8 Redox Reactions

from_notes: Red litmus No change Blue
x: Red litmus turns blue only with a base. No change means the liquid is not a base, but it could be an acid or neutral, so only option 1 must be true.

from_notes: Carbon dioxide (CO2) + Lime water [Ca(OH)2] -> Calcium Carbonate (CaCO3) + Water
x: CO2 reacts with lime water (calcium hydroxide) to form insoluble calcium carbonate, which makes it milky.
Nitric acid decomposes in light to give brown NO2, which dissolves in the acid and gives it a yellow colour.
source: NCERT Chemistry Class 12 ch.7 p-Block (nitric acid decomposition)

from_notes: Urea, Ammonium sulphate, Ammonium nitrate, Calcium ammonium nitrate
x: Ammonium nitrate, phosphate and sulphate supply nitrogen or phosphorus to crops and are fertilisers. Ammonium sulphide is not used as one.
Cutting an onion releases alliinase (synthase), which converts amino acid sulfoxides into sulfenic acids; these form the tear-inducing compound.
source: Nature 419:685 (2002) Imai et al. 'An onion enzyme that makes the eyes water' (sulfenic acid); printed key SSC CGL 2020

x: Souring forms lactic acid by bacterial fermentation, so the acidity rises and the pH falls below 6.
source: NCERT Science Class 10 ch.2 Acids, Bases and Salts (pH of milk falls as it turns to curd)

from_notes: Photoelectric effect Heinrich Hertz (1887); explained by Einstein
x: Emission of electrons from a metal surface by incident light is the photoelectric effect. Thermionic emission is caused by heat.
In parallel the equivalent resistance is less than the smallest resistor. 1/R = 1/2+1/4+1/8 = 7/8, so R = 8/7 Ω, which is less than 2 Ω.

from_notes: Reactivity Series (high to low): K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Pb > [H] > Cu > Hg > Ag > Au
x: Mercury lies below hydrogen in the reactivity series, so it cannot displace hydrogen from dilute HCl. Al, Mg and Fe lie above hydrogen and release H2.

from_notes: Chlorophyll -> Magnesium (Mg)
x: Chlorophyll has magnesium at the centre of its porphyrin ring.
Na+ and O2− both have 10 electrons, so they are isoelectronic. In the other pairs the electron counts differ.
source: NCERT Chemistry Class 11 ch.3 Classification of Elements (isoelectronic species)

x: In 2HgO → 2Hg + O2, mercury(II) oxide loses oxygen and Hg is reduced from +2 to 0. The other reactions are oxidation or combination reactions.
source: NCERT Science Class 10 ch.1 / ch.3 (reduction = loss of oxygen; HgO heated gives Hg)

from_notes: Reactivity Series (high to low): K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Pb > [H] > Cu > Hg > Ag > Au
x: In the reactivity series the order is Na > Mg > Zn > Cu, with sodium most reactive and copper least.
In series the resistances add up, Rs = R1+R2+..., so the net resistance increases.
source: NCERT Science Class 10 ch.12 Electricity (Rs = R1 + R2 + R3)

from_notes: Inside the solenoid, the magnetic field is uniform and strong
x: Inside a solenoid the magnetic field is uniform, with parallel field lines, so it remains the same.

from_notes: Ciliary Muscles Change lens curvature
x: A thinner eye lens is less converging, so its focal length increases. A thicker lens has a shorter focal length.

from_notes: Hertz (frequency) Heinrich Hertz
x: Hertz is the SI unit of frequency, equal to one cycle per second.

from_notes: Metals are good conductors of heat and electricity.
x: Metal is a good conductor, so it draws heat from the hand quickly and feels colder than plastic, a poor conductor, at the same temperature.

from_notes: Natural polymers: Proteins (amino acids) ... Silk, Wool
x: Wool is made of the protein keratin, whereas cotton and jute are cellulose and rubber is a hydrocarbon polymer.

from_notes: Bakelite (first synthetic plastic)
x: Bakelite, made from phenol and formaldehyde, was the first fully synthetic plastic and is a poor conductor of heat and electricity, so it is used for handles and switches. Polythene, nylon and Teflon came later.

from_notes: Lysosomes ... they are also known as the 'suicide bags' of a cell.
x: Lysosomes are called 'suicidal bags' because their hydrolytic enzymes can digest the cell itself when the cell is damaged or dies.
Red, green and blue are the primary colours of light, and mixing all three gives white light.
Mixing red and green light gives yellow, as in additive colour mixing.
source: Britannica 'Additive colour mixing' (red + green light = yellow)

x: The primary colours of light, used in photography, are red, green and blue. Yellow and cyan are secondary colours.
source: Britannica 'Additive colour mixing' (RGB primaries of light, used in photography)

from_notes: Flowering plants or angiosperms undergo a unique process called double fertilisation.
x: Double fertilisation, in which one sperm fuses with the egg and the other with the polar nuclei, is unique to angiosperms.

from_notes: Parthenocarpic Fruits: Fruits formed without fertilisation, like bananas, are seedless.
x: Parthenocarpy is the development of fruit without fertilisation, giving seedless fruit. Parthenogenesis is the development of an embryo from an unfertilised egg, not of a fruit.

from_notes: Parthenocarpic Fruits: Fruits formed without fertilisation, like bananas, are seedless.
x: Parthenocarpy is fruit development without fertilisation. Apomixis is seed formation without fertilisation, so it is not the answer.
In plant sexual reproduction, pollination is followed by fertilisation, then division of the zygote, embryo formation and finally the seedling.
source: NCERT Science Class 10 ch.8 How do Organisms Reproduce

from_notes: Amoeba Protista
x: Amoeba is a unicellular eukaryote, so it belongs to Kingdom Protista, not Monera, which holds prokaryotes.

from_notes: Meristematic tissue is responsible for plant growth. It consists of undifferentiated cells that can divide
x: Meristematic tissue is made of actively dividing cells, and its cell division drives plant growth. It is not dead and is not limited to bark.

from_notes: Sclerenchyma cells have thick, lignified (hardened) walls. These cells are usually dead
x: Sclerenchyma cells have thick lignified walls and are dead at maturity. Epidermis, parenchyma and collenchyma are living tissues.

from_notes: Lysosomes are membrane-bound sacs filled with digestive enzymes
x: Lysosomes contain hydrolytic (digestive) enzymes that break down macromolecules and worn-out cell parts.

from_notes: Esters Fruity smell Perfumes, flavouring agents
x: Ethyl acetate is an ester, and esters have sweet, fruity smells. Methyl chloride, methanoic acid and methanol do not smell fruity.

from_notes: fungi have cell walls made of chitin (a complex sugar), unlike plants, which have cellulose
x: Fungal cell walls are made mainly of chitin, not purely cellulose, so the statement that all fungi have a purely cellulosic wall is wrong.

from_notes: Abscisic Acid (ABA): Inhibits growth and promotes seed dormancy and leaf senescence.
x: Abscisic acid is the stress hormone. It closes stomata and so helps the plant tolerate drought.

from_notes: Lysosomes are membrane-bound sacs filled with digestive enzymes
x: Lysosomes store digestive enzymes, and this is why they are called 'suicidal bags'. Ribosomes make proteins, and desmosomes are cell junctions.

from_notes: Bacteria Monera
x: Bacteria are prokaryotes and belong to Monera. Mushrooms and yeast are fungi, and moss is a bryophyte.

from_notes: Seed Dispersal
x: Seeds are dispersed by wind, water and animals. Fungi do not disperse seeds.

from_notes: The black coating on silver and the green coating on copper are other examples of corrosion.
x: In moist air copper reacts with CO2, oxygen and water to form a green coat of basic copper carbonate (the patina of the Statue of Liberty). Copper oxide is black and copper sulphate is blue.

from_notes: Maximum water absorbed by plants Root hairs
x: Root hairs are the main water-absorbing part of the root; water enters them by osmosis from the soil, so they absorb the most water for the plant.

from_notes: Mitochondria have their own DNA and ribosomes, allowing them to produce some of their proteins.
x: Mitochondria contain their own small circular DNA, apart from nuclear DNA. Centrioles, Golgi apparatus and lysosomes do not carry DNA.

from_notes: Mitochondria have their own DNA and ribosomes, allowing them to produce some of their proteins.
x: Mitochondria have their own DNA and ribosomes, so they can synthesise some of their own proteins. They cannot make a nucleus, chloroplasts or digestive enzymes.

from_notes: Theory of Natural Selection / Darwinism Charles Darwin
x: Natural selection, proposed by Darwin, is the main driving mechanism of evolution. Mutation only supplies variation, and acquired characters are not inherited.

from_notes: Artificial sources are ultrasonic transducers and piezoelectric crystals.
x: Ultrasonic waves are generated by the piezoelectric effect: a quartz crystal vibrates at high frequency when an alternating voltage is applied to it.
Parallel currents in the same direction produce magnetic fields that make the wires attract each other; opposite currents would repel.
source: NCERT Physics Class 12 ch.4 Moving Charges and Magnetism

x: Ethane has a C-C single bond (about 154 pm), longer than the double bond in ethene, the triple bond in ethyne or the intermediate bond in benzene.
source: NCERT Chemistry Class 11 ch.13 Hydrocarbons (bond lengths)

x: Animal cells have no cell wall, so animal bodies do not contain cellulose; cellulose is a plant feature. Animals cannot make their own food, lack chlorophyll and can move about.
source: NCERT Science Class 9 ch.7 Diversity in Living Organisms (animals: no cell wall)

from_notes: Ohm's Law applies primarily to ohmic materials
x: An ohmic conductor obeys Ohm's law (V proportional to I). Metals like silver do; semiconductors such as germanium and silicon and carbon do not follow it.
Conductivity is the reciprocal of resistivity (σ = 1/ρ), so their product is always 1 for every conductor.
source: NCERT Physics Class 12 ch.3 Current Electricity (σ = 1/ρ)

from_notes: Electrical Conductivity: Metals are good conductors of electricity due to free electrons.
x: Metals have free electrons and are good conductors of electricity, so they carry current with little loss; this is why household wires are metal.

from_notes: mitochondria are known as the powerhouses of the cell
x: Mitochondria release energy as ATP by cellular respiration, so they are called the powerhouses of the cell.

from_notes: Analogous Structures: Different structures with the same function, like bird and butterfly wings
x: Analogous organs have different structure and origin but perform similar functions, such as the wings of a bird and an insect. Homologous organs have the same structure but different functions.

from_notes: Antipyretic Reduces fever Aspirin, Paracetamol
x: Antipyretics such as paracetamol reduce high fever. Antiseptics act on living tissue against microbes and antibiotics kill bacteria.

from_notes: Mammals have a four-chambered heart and breathe through the lungs.
x: A whale is a mammal living in water, so it breathes air with lungs and not gills.
Metastasis is the spread of cancer cells through blood or lymph to other organs.
source: NCERT Biology Class 12 ch.8 Human Health and Disease (cancer)

from_notes: Adipose Tissue: It comprises fat cells (adipocytes)
x: Adipocytes are the fat-storing cells of adipose connective tissue. Chondrocytes are in cartilage and osteocytes in bone.
Mescaline comes from the peyote cactus, not from Thea chinensis (tea), whose leaves yield caffeine. So the pair is mismatched.
source: NCERT Biology Class 12 ch.8 Human Health and Disease (drugs and their sources)

x: Cyanide inhibits cytochrome c oxidase, which blocks the electron transport chain. Cells then cannot make ATP, so death is very quick.
source: Standard biochemistry (cyanide inhibits cytochrome c oxidase of the ETC)

x: Earthworms (red worms) have a muscular gizzard that grinds food with the help of small stones.
source: NCERT Biology Class 11 ch.7 Structural Organisation in Animals (earthworm gizzard)

x: Metformin is a standard oral anti-diabetic drug (it lowers blood glucose); zolpidem is a sleep aid, promethazine an antihistamine and hydralazine an antihypertensive.
source: Standard pharmacology (metformin – first-line oral drug for type 2 diabetes)

from_notes: Analgesic Pain relief
x: Analgesics are pain-relieving drugs; antipyretics reduce fever, antibiotics kill bacteria and antiseptics are applied on living tissue to prevent infection.
Physalia is the Portuguese man of war (4), Taenia is a tapeworm (3), Fasciola is the liver fluke (1) and Scypha (Sycon) is a sponge (2), giving 4 3 1 2.
source: NCERT Biology Class 11 ch.4 Animal Kingdom

x: Bacteria, viruses and fungi multiply rapidly in large numbers, whereas worms reproduce sexually and much more slowly.
source: Standard microbiology; printed key SSC 2018, not verified

from_notes: Mammals have a four-chambered heart and breathe through the lungs.
x: Mammals have a four-chambered heart; a three-chambered heart is found in amphibians and most reptiles. The other statements hold (hair, egg-laying monotremes, aquatic whales).

from_notes: Fundamental Quantities: These are physical quantities that are not derived from other quantities
x: Length, time and mass are fundamental quantities; weight is a force (mg), a derived quantity that varies with gravity.

from_notes: Diatomic molecules: They consist of two atoms
x: Iodine exists as diatomic I2 molecules, whereas copper, helium and barium occur as single atoms (monoatomic).

from_notes: Cinchona Bark Quinine
x: Morphine comes from the poppy plant, tetracycline from bacteria (Streptomyces), quinine from cinchona bark and penicillin from the fungus Penicillium, giving 2 4 1 3.

from_notes: 1 Å (angstrom) = 10⁻¹⁰ m
x: The angstrom is 10⁻¹⁰ m, a unit of length used for wavelengths and atomic sizes. Energy is in joules or eV, frequency in hertz, velocity in m/s.

from_notes: Pleiotropy
x: Pleiotropy is when a single gene affects two or more characters; apomixis is seed formation without fertilisation, polyploidy is extra chromosome sets and polyteny is repeated DNA strands in giant chromosomes.

from_notes: Dicots (with two cotyledons...)
x: Pulses (legumes) have two cotyledons so they are dicots; rice, wheat and maize are monocot cereals.

from_notes: Virus trap Vegetative propagation can also transmit plant viruses
x: Vegetative propagation gives clones (I) and can be done through much of the year (III). It does not eliminate viruses, since the virus passes on to the offspring, so II is wrong.
In photosynthesis, water is split and oxygen is released as the by-product; sugar is the main product, and CO2 is a raw material.
source: NCERT Biology Class 11 ch.13 Photosynthesis (O2 released from water)

from_notes: W (Tungsten) Hardest metal
x: Among the options, tungsten is the hardest metal; it also has the highest melting point.
Cloves are the dried unopened flower buds of the clove tree (Syzygium aromaticum).
source: Spices Board India / standard botany (clove = flower bud)

from_notes: Earliest known Cro-Magnon remains ~30,000–45,000 years old
x: Cro-Magnon man was the most recent of these and was essentially anatomically modern Homo sapiens; Java, Peking and Neanderthal men were earlier.
Starch gives a blue-black colour with iodine, but cellulose does not. Both are plant-origin glucose polymers.
source: NCERT Biology Class 11 ch.9 Biomolecules (starch–iodine blue; cellulose does not)

x: Zoology is the study of animals, both living and dead (fossils, preserved specimens); botany deals with plants.
source: Standard definition (zoology: animals living and extinct)

x: Evolutionary order of appearance: amphibian (salamander), then reptile (python), then mammal (kangaroo). The other sequences are not in evolutionary order.

from_notes: Cooling by ice High latent heat of fusion -> absorbs large heat
x: Ice absorbs latent heat of fusion from the drink while melting, which lowers the drink's temperature, so R correctly explains A.
Venomous snake fangs are modified maxillary teeth, borne on the maxilla of the upper jaw. They are not mandibular (lower jaw), palatine or canine teeth; snakes have no canines.
source: Britannica 'Snake: fangs' (fangs on the maxillary bone)

from_notes: Mass (m) Inertia / amount of matter (scalar, constant)
